title: Osero's emergency response protocols are entirely unwritten for both ecosystem-wide and Agent-only situations
content:
Two adjacent documents in the Omni section define Osero's emergency posture and then supply nothing. A.6.1.1.7.3.1.2, Sky Ecosystem Emergency Response, covers "situations that impact the entire Sky Ecosystem" and states: "This protocol will be specified in a future iteration of the Osero Artifact." A.6.1.1.7.3.1.3, Agent-Specific Emergency Response, covers "situations solely impacting Osero versus the broader Sky Ecosystem" — same deferral.

The gap is narrower than it first appears but still substantial. Osero does have emergency procedures *within* Primitives: the accelerated Root Edit at A.6.1.1.7.2.2.2.2.1.2.3.1, and the Liquidity Layer's revoke-withdraw-burn sequence at A.6.1.1.7.2.6.1.2.2.3. What is missing is the Agent-level layer that would coordinate them, decide which applies, or handle an emergency that is not a governance action or a liquidity-layer compromise.

The distinction the empty sections draw is itself informative. Separating ecosystem-wide from Osero-only emergencies asserts that the two require different responses — plausibly because an ecosystem-wide event may demand Osero act against its own local interest, while an Osero-only event is its own to resolve. The taxonomy is set even though the content is not.

Read against the same Artifact's very specific liquidity-layer emergency machinery, the contrast suggests the drafting priority: mechanisms that need onchain wiring and named multisigs were specified first, and the coordinating judgment layer was left for later.
description: A.6.1.1.7.3.1.2 and .1.3 name the two cases and defer both to future iterations, so the Agent has emergency procedures only inside specific Primitives.
